name: pdk-nodestream-pipeline
instr:
We load our logistics vendor's nightly drop into the inventory graph with `nodestream run manifests --target graph --storage-backend checkpoints`. A copy of the project that writes to the null database, with a sample drop, is in /data/inventory.

When a run fails part way, running it again starts over at the first file and writes everything again. Some nights the rerun dies in the same place as well.

A rerun with the same storage backend should pick up where the failed run stopped. An input record (a JSON line, a CSV row, or a whole .json document) whose output all got through every step of the pipeline before the failure is not read again. Every other input record is sent again in full, including one whose output only partly got through. Nothing may be lost or sent twice beyond that, whichever step failed, whatever steps the pipeline has, and whatever --step-outbox-size is. Files added to the drop after the failure are loaded by the rerun, and if the rerun fails too, the next run continues from there. A file that can't be read is skipped, the rest of the drop still loads and the run succeeds. After a run that finishes without a fatal error, the next run loads everything again. Runs without --storage-backend behave as they do now.

Please find what's wrong and fix it. The existing tests in /app/tests must keep passing. There's no network access, and nodestream with its dependencies is installed.
